title: Final integration
instructions: Choose the architecture that protects privacy, proves eligibility, and prevents double voting.
successCriteria: Select the private witness, ZK proof, Merkle root, and nullifier architecture.

stages.title: Private witness
stages.description: Keep eligibility and private voter data hidden while preparing the proof.

pieces.label: Keep eligibility data in the private witness
Publish the raw voter identity for everyone to inspect
Copy the witness into a public ledger field

stages.explanation: The witness contains private eligibility data, so it must remain hidden instead of becoming public state.

stages.title: Merkle membership
stages.description: Prove that the private witness belongs to the authorized Merkle root.

pieces.label: Verify a Merkle path against the authorized root
Publish every voter identity as the membership proof
Compare the witness only with the current vote count

stages.explanation: A Merkle membership path links the hidden witness to the authorized root without revealing the entire voter set.

stages.title: Zero-knowledge proof
stages.description: Prove eligibility without revealing the witness itself.

pieces.label: Generate a ZK proof of eligibility without exposing the witness
Reveal the witness so the verifier can check it directly
Trust the submitted claim without cryptographic evidence

stages.explanation: The ZK proof lets the system verify the claim while keeping the witness value private.

stages.title: Nullifier
stages.description: Prevent the same eligibility from being used twice.

pieces.label: Derive a nullifier and reject any repeated nullifier
Reveal the witness whenever the voter submits again
Accept every proof even when the eligibility repeats

stages.explanation: The nullifier marks one use of an eligibility without exposing its source, allowing the system to reject reuse.

payload.finalSummary: The complete architecture keeps the witness private, proves Merkle membership, uses a ZK proof to verify eligibility without disclosure, and checks a nullifier to prevent double use.
